acceptance_criteria_mapping.AC1: src/app/features/facility/components/containers/combined-structure/combined-structure.component.html adds a fourth resizer bar (`.resizer.resizer--vertical`, data-testid="combined-tree-height-resizer") between the electrical and mechanical `<cdm-dual-tree>` panels inside `.main__trees`, with `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation="horizontal"` (correct per WAI-ARIA APG Window Splitter pattern: the bar is a horizontal line dragged vertically), `tabindex="0"`, `aria-label`, and dynamic `aria-valuemin/valuenow/valuemax` bound to `treeHeightResizerAriaValues()`. combined-structure.component.ts adds `onTreeHeightResizerKeyDown` (ArrowUp/ArrowDown, 24px step) and orientation-aware `onResizerMouseDown`/`resizePanelsByOffset`/`getMinHeight`. Proven by: unit test 'resizes tree panel height via keyboard arrow keys on the separator' (combined-structure.component.spec.ts:409) and identically-named Playwright test in combined-structure-tree-height-resize.e2e.spec.ts:51, plus 'resizes tree panel height via vertical drag handle' (e2e spec:76). Both the assigned unit test and the e2e spec file name appear verbatim in the diff.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.AC2: Same drag-to-resize mechanism as the existing width resizers is generalized (shared `startDrag`/`resizePanelsByOffset`, orientation resolved via `data-resize-axis="y"`) rather than a parallel implementation. Proven by: e2e test 'drag handle updates electrical and mechanical tree heights independently' (combined-structure-tree-height-resize.e2e.spec.ts:86), which drags +260px then -320px and asserts both panels' heights move independently and correctly in each direction.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.AC3: `getMinHeight`/`getMinSize` reads each `cdm-dual-tree` panel's computed `min-height` (180px, set via `--combined-tree-panel-min-height` in combined-structure.component.scss) and `resizePanelsByOffset` clamps the drag/keyboard offset so neither panel's size can go below its minimum. Proven by: e2e test 'clamps tree panel height at configured minimum during drag' (combined-structure-tree-height-resize.e2e.spec.ts:101), which drags -2000px and +4000px and asserts each panel is clamped at its configured min-height (with 1px tolerance).

remaining_gaps.detail: Visual focus-indicator appearance/contrast for the new separator (WCAG 2.4.7) could not be screenshotted or manually Tab-navigated this session because the interactive Playwright-browser MCP tool (navigate/press_key/resize) denied permission on every attempt, including against an already-loaded blank tab. Code inspection found no CSS rule suppressing the outline for `.resizer`/`.resizer--vertical` or globally in styles.scss/utilities.scss, so the browser's native focus ring should render by default (native-before-ARIA, no color-only reliance) — but this is reasoning from markup, not an exercised observation, so it is reported as unverified rather than assumed passing, per this repository's own review policy.

Home/End keyboard shortcuts (jump to min/max) are not implemented on the new separator. This is an APG-recommended enhancement for the Window Splitter pattern, not a WCAG success-criterion requirement, and is not named in any assigned test_id — flagged as a non-blocking future enhancement, not a defect.

The pre-existing three horizontal (width) resizer bars still carry no `role`/`aria-orientation`/keyboard support at all (unchanged by this PR). The approved plan (§4.7) explicitly scoped retrofitting them as optional ('do not expand scope to rework them if it is not trivial'), so this is a documented pre-existing gap, not a regression introduced here.

The shipped minimum tree-panel height is 180px (`--combined-tree-panel-min-height` in combined-structure.component.scss), not the 150px value the approved plan (§4.5) explicitly decided and instructed the implementer to ship as-is unless a documented usability defect justified a change. No commit message or PR text records the reason for this deviation, though the plan's own risk section requires such a change to be 'recorded... as evidence.' This is a process/documentation gap for the caller to note, not an accessibility defect — 180px is strictly larger (more generous) than 150px, so it does not weaken usability or a11y.
